stories.title: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway
stories.excerpt: AmTrustRE has signed the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) to 39,000 square feet at 250 Broadway for its new headquarters. Occupancy is expected in Q1 2027. “We’re proud to welcome the Taxi and Limousine Commission to 250 Broadway as they establish their new headquarters,” said Jonathan Bennett, president of AmTrustRE. “Our relationship with the City of New York spans multiple leases across our portfolio, and this lease builds on that long-standing partnership. As we continue to invest in and elevate 250 Broadway, TLC’s decision to make this building their home reflects the building’s premier location, modern infrastructure, and enduring appeal to institutional tenants.” AmTrustRE was represented by Anne Holker in-house, along with Brad Gerla, Michael Rizzo, and Alex Benisatto of CBRE as landlord broker. The tenant was represented by Gus Field of Cushman & Wakefield. The post NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYC TLC signs 39,000 sf at 250 Broadway, occupancy Q1 2027.
Institutional tenant lease reinforces AmTrustRE's lower Manhattan office portfolio.
Government agency relocation supports FiDi office market stabilization.
stories.summary: AmTrustRE leased 39,000 square feet at 250 Broadway to NYC's Taxi and Limousine Commission, with occupancy expected in Q1 2027. The deal reflects sustained demand from institutional tenants for modern lower Manhattan office space. This is primarily an office transaction with limited direct relevance to multifamily development.
stories.impact: Minimal impact to multifamily development. Government tenant consolidation in lower Manhattan does not signal residential demand shifts or affect apartment market fundamentals in NYC's core residential submarkets.

stories.title: Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed the $8,500,000 sale of a multifamily complex located at 1775 Beloit Av. in West Los Angeles. Vice chair Kitty Wallace represented both the buyer, UCLA Housing Group, and the seller, Enterprise Bank. The sale was completed through a court-appointed receivership process. UCLA Housing Group plans to convert the property into student housing. Constructed in 2023, the seven-story, Type II co-living property comprises approximately 18,000 square feet and 16 residential units totaling 48 beds. The transaction closed at $531,250 per unit, or approximately $472 per square foot. “The transaction reflects a broader shift underway across the Los Angeles multifamily market,” said Wallace. “Over the past decade, developers increasingly delivered co-living communities to provide attainable housing near the region’s largest employment and education centers. Following the pandemic, however, Los Angeles experienced a prolonged period of muted rent growth while household incomes, replacement costs, and home prices continued to climb. As new development has become increasingly difficult and the forward construction pipeline continues to contract, investors are placing greater emphasis on acquiring well-located existing assets below replacement cost in anticipation of improving supply-demand fundamentals.” The post Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: UCLA Housing Group acquires 2023-built co-living property, West LA, $8.5M.
16-unit co-living conversion to student housing reflects demand shift away from co-living.
Market commentary: LA multifamily stalled on muted rent growth vs. rising replacement costs.
stories.summary: Colliers closed the $8.5M sale of a 16-unit, 18,000 sf co-living complex at 1775 Beloit Avenue (built 2023) to UCLA Housing Group, which will convert it to student housing. Transaction priced at $531,250 per unit and $472/sf. The sale signals a pivot: co-living demand has weakened in LA as pandemic rent stagnation, rising construction costs, and elevated home prices made forward development economically difficult.
stories.impact: In West LA and broader Los Angeles, developer appetite for new multifamily (especially co-living) is collapsing—forward pipeline contraction means tighter supply growth and potential rent upside as existing stock absorbs demand without new competitive pressure. However, UCLA's institutional buyout suggests student-focused housing remains resilient. Watch for co-living asset distress sales as cap rates compress valuations.

stories.title: Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets closed the $23.5-million sale of 1150 Broadway, a residential development site in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn. The team of Brendan Maddigan, Steve Rutman, Mike Mazzara and Ethan Stanton represented the seller, A-PLUS International Realty, and negotiated directly with the buyers, Brooklyn-based YS Developers and Rabsky Group. Situated at the crossroads of Bedford-Stuyvesant and Bushwick, the 26,730-square-foot corner site is zoned for a mixed-use building with apartments, local retail and community facilities. Under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity program, it offers up to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right zoning floor area. The property also sits within a federally designated Qualified Opportunity Zone and is eligible for the 485-x tax abatement program. The site features approximately 475 feet of wraparound frontage along Lafayette Avenue, Kosciuszko Street, Kossuth Place and Broadway. “Sites with this much frontage, this level of zoning flexibility and direct subway access rarely come to market in Brooklyn, and our marketing process generated significant interest from developers looking to establish a presence in the neighborhood,” said Maddigan. “YS Developers and Rabsky Group have a clear path to deliver a large-scale residential project with an attractive long-term position. The post Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: YS Developers and Rabsky Group acquire Brooklyn dev site, $23.5M, Bed-Stuy/Bushwick.
26,730 sf corner lot zoned for 133,917 sf mixed-use under City of Yes; 485-x abatement eligible.
475 feet wraparound frontage, direct subway access, rare entitlement velocity.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets sold 1150 Broadway, a 26,730 sf mixed-use development site in the Bedford-Stuyvesant/Bushwick boundary, to Brooklyn-based YS Developers and Rabsky Group for $23.5M. The site benefits from City of Yes for Housing Opportunity zoning (up to 133,917 sf), 485-x tax abatement eligibility, Qualified Opportunity Zone status, and exceptional wraparound corner frontage (475 feet) with direct subway access.
stories.impact: Bed-Stuy/Bushwick is attracting significant developer capital and aggressive bid-down competition driven by rare rezoned entitlements under City of Yes. This signals strong forward demand for residential development in outer-borough Brooklyn submarkets with infrastructure and tax incentives. Developers acquiring now can realize rapid value creation post-entitlement; rising land prices will squeeze future development feasibility in the neighborhood.

stories.title: Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors and Progressive Real Estate Partners arranged the $2.64-million sale of a renovated, single‑tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield. The building, originally constructed in 2013, underwent a full renovation in 2025 and is leased to AutoZone on a new 15‑year triple-net lease. EVP and partner Jeff Lefko and EVP Bill Asher of Hanley represented the seller, Torrey Financial Group, based in San Diego. The buyer, a private investor from Los Angeles, was represented by Greg Bedell, SVP and Managing Director, and Lance Mordachini, Vice President with Progressive Real Estate Partners in Rancho Cucamonga. “We procured an all‑cash, 1031-exchange buyer from Nevada,” said Lefko. “We negotiated a 40‑day escrow and closed at over 96% of the listing price, which reflects the continued depth of demand for essential retail in fast‑growing suburban markets.” Bedell added, “Our buyer was highly motivated and moved quickly because of the long‑term lease, the recent renovation, replaceable rent, and the investment grade strength of AutoZone. This asset checked every box for investors seeking stable, service‑based retail in supply‑constrained California markets.” The AutoZone is located at 1125 Olive Dr. in Bakersfield, occupying an 8,302‑square‑foot building. The post Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Single-tenant AutoZone sold in Bakersfield, $2.64M, 15-year NNN lease.
1031-exchange buyer highlights depth of essential retail demand in suburban CA.
No direct multifamily signal; supply-constrained retail market.
stories.summary: Hanley Investment Group and Progressive Real Estate Partners closed the $2.64M sale of a renovated single-tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield on a new 15-year triple-net lease. The all-cash buyer, a Nevada-based 1031-exchange investor, was attracted to lease duration, recent renovation, and AutoZone's investment-grade credit. The deal closed at 96% of list price in a 40-day escrow.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Single-tenant retail in fast-growing suburban markets (Bakersfield) is experiencing strong investor demand, but this reflects essential services (auto parts) demand and cap-rate compression in retail NNN, not residential supply/demand dynamics.

stories.title: Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors
stories.excerpt: Resource Realty of Northern New Jersey arranged the sale of a high-utility, standalone industrial facility located at 36 Pine St.in Rockaway, NJ. The transaction was brokered and finalized by firm Principals Greg Sabato and Scott Peck, who represented the buyer, Commerce Park Investors. The property encompasses 53,252 square feet of functional industrial space. Suitable for intensive manufacturing, assembly or specialized logistics, the building features heavy-duty infrastructure, including two tailboard exterior dock doors and one drive-in bay. Crucial for modern industrial users, the property boasts heavy power, equipped with a 2,500 amp, 440-volt electrical system capable of supporting heavy production loads. “This single-story property represents a unique opportunity for an operator requiring significant power infrastructure wrapped in a highly functional industrial footprint,” said Sabato. “Heavy power of this caliber – 2,500 amps – coupled with dedicated loading capabilities is an increasingly rare commodity in the northern New Jersey market. Securing this building underscores the sustained demand for spaces that can immediately accommodate a full-range of manufacturing and technical requirements.”  The post Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Commerce Park Investors acquire 53,252 sf industrial facility, Rockaway NJ, heavy power.
2,500 amp, 440-volt infrastructure; two dock doors, one drive-in bay.
High-utility industrial footprint reflects scarcity of heavy power in northern NJ.
stories.summary: Resource Realty of Northern New Jersey brokered the sale of a 53,252 sf standalone industrial facility at 36 Pine Street in Rockaway to Commerce Park Investors. The single-story building features heavy power (2,500 amps at 440 volts), two tailboard dock doors, and one drive-in bay, making it suitable for intensive manufacturing or specialized logistics.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Industrial real estate scarcity in northern NJ reflects logistics/manufacturing demand and supply constraints in the region, but does not affect apartment market supply, demand, or capital flows.

stories.title: Arrow Real Estate Advisors Hires Jeff Weinberg as Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors is adding another experienced veteran to its staff of capital markets experts. The New York-based real estate advisory firm has hired Jeffrey Weinberg as a managing director, Commercial Observer can first report. Weinberg comes from Meridian Capital Group, a firm he co-founded in 1991. Weinberg served as executive vice president, specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. “Jeff has built an exceptional career in commercial real estate and has an unparalleled depth of knowledge and relationships across the industry,” said Morris Betesh, founder of Arrow Real Estate Advisors. “His experience, judgment and entrepreneurial approach align perfectly with Arrow’s platform and culture.” Weinberg’s move is not uncommon. Betesh, previously a senior managing director at Meridian Capital Group, had exited the firm along with 12 team members to form his own capital markets advisory firm. Weinberg told CO that he joined Arrow Real Estate mainly due to the strength of his relationship with Betesh, whom he worked with at Meridian Capital Group for several years. “Morris and I were friends over there, we worked together at the old place, he left a couple of years ago, and I thought this would be a nice fit for me in this stage of life and my career,” said Weinberg. Weinberg was one of the original founding partners at Meridian Capital Group, where his expertise during a three-decade tenure ran from managing client and lender relationships to executing CRE transactions across developments and strategic relationships. He estimated that he has completed more than $1 billion in originations in his career. He told CO that he was attracted to Arrow Real Estate’s ongoing growth and expansion since the company was founded in October 2024. “I knew Morris had a very good team of professionals who know the market very well and I thought it would be a good fit to make my next move,” he said. bullets: Arrow Real Estate Advisors hires Jeff Weinberg as managing director from Meridian.

stories.summary: Arrow Real Estate Advisors hired Jeffrey Weinberg as managing director. stories.impact: Indirect signal of multifamily debt market fragmentation: senior talent exiting large lenders (Meridian) and gravitating to smaller advisory platforms (Arrow) suggests lenders are consolidating and boutique platforms are capturing market share. For developers, this may indicate tighter CMBS/debt availability and rising advisory costs, though specialty debt expertise (multifamily focus) is in demand.

stories.title: Alexandria Shows Positive Signs After Several Depressed Quarters: Earnings
stories.excerpt: Ailing Alexandria Real Estate Equities is showing signs of improvement as leasing increased over the second quarter of 2026, a hopeful sign of progress after several quarters of declining fundamentals. The life sciences-focused real estate investment trust (REIT) posted earnings Tuesday that show declining balance sheet performance with $73.7 million in net income for the second quarter of 2026 versus $109.6 million during the same period last year. Funds from operations (FFO) was $296.1 million, more than $100 million lighter than in the second quarter of 2025 and down a similar amount from the $396.4 million reported in the first quarter of 2026. Revenue declined from $762 million in the second quarter of last year to $662.7 million for the same period in 2026. Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, however, was more optimistic than in previous quarters, stating that science sectors are improving economically, even if that progress has not yet been reflected on the real estate side. “We’re winning an outsized number of shares of transactions, which is good,” Marcus said during the call. “We have a very well-diversified and strong tenant base. … Very strong leasing in the second quarter from our life science products, service and device sector really depicts shovels and tools of the industry and is almost 40 percent of the leasing volume.” Alexandria leased 1 million square feet of space in the second quarter of 2026, compared to about 647,300 square feet in the first quarter, with about 329,000 square feet being deals that backfilled newly vacant space. In previous quarters, Alexandria executives have pursued dispositions to support the company financially while the life science market recovers. The company sold $170.3 million in assets, including 3825 and 3875 Fabian Way in Palo Alto, Calif., for $163 million in mid-July. bullets: Alexandria Real Estate Equities Q2 2026: FFO $296.1M, down >$100M YoY.
Life sciences REIT showing leasing improvement but revenue declined $99M YoY.
CEO optimistic on science sector recovery despite lagging real estate fundamentals.
stories.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities reported Q2 2026 earnings showing FFO of $296.1M (down >$100M YoY) and revenue of $662.7M (down $99M YoY), with net income at $73.7M versus $109.6M in Q2 2025. However, leasing activity increased in Q2, and CEO Joel Marcus expressed optimism that science sectors are improving economically, signaling potential future REIT recovery.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Life sciences REIT fundamentals reflect sector-specific headwinds (biotech funding, R&D spending) and are largely orthogonal to apartment market dynamics. No signal on residential demand, supply, or capital deployment.

stories.title: Munish Viralam of Newmark: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Munish Viralam arrived at Newmark in June, fresh off an 18-year stint at CBRE. As executive vice chairman at Newmark, Viralam has been tasked with leading the firm’s newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group, scaling up its strategic arm, and helping corporate tenants navigate the maze-like process of real estate strategy and negotiations. Viralam found his niche at Emory University, where degrees in finance and real estate placed him at an intriguing crossroads between the business world and entrepreneurship. He landed a job at CBRE after graduation, where he proceeded to spend nearly two decades honing his craft as a real estate strategist and problem solver. Viralam was serving as executive vice president in charge of CBRE’s consulting group in Manhattan when Newmark came a-knocking. Commercial Observer sat down with Viralam in July, just a few weeks into his tenure at Newmark, to discuss his vision for the group, New York’s office occupancy challenges and where real estate consulting slots into the dealmaking mix. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you describe the nature of the real estate strategy and consulting group’s work? Where does it fit into Newmark’s broader deal-making? Munish Viralam: We called it the real estate strategy and consulting group because we want to emphasize both of those components of what the practice is. It is a transactional-based group and it’s focused on advising large corporate entities within New York City on their real estate and occupancy strategies. It’s a pretty analytical approach, if you will, but that doesn’t just mean numbers. It means assessing all of the risks and the pros of strategies that we could pursue. The idea is to become a strategic hub for the organization. stories.summary: Munish Viralam, who spent 18 years at CBRE as executive vice president overseeing the consulting group in Manhattan, joined Newmark in June 2026 as executive vice chairman. He was hired to lead Newmark's newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group and help corporate tenants navigate real estate strategy and negotiations.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Viralam's hire reflects corporate real estate consulting demand (office leasing, corporate strategy) and talent competition among brokerage platforms, but does not signal residential market dynamics, supply, or capital trends.

stories.title: Prologis’ European Rival Segro Accepts $18.8B Takeover Offer
stories.excerpt: Prologis, the world’s largest industrial landlord, is about to get even bigger. The San Francisco-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has succeeded in its fourth offer to acquire rival Segro, the United Kingdom’s largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro’s equity at roughly $18.8 billion. Prologis announced Tuesday that Segro’s once-resistant board would be recommending the deal. The combined portfolios’ global platform will total approximately $269 billion of assets under management. For the U.K., the deal means losing its largest REIT, the history of which stretches back more than a century. Segro’s portfolio spans approximately 117 million square feet across the U.K. and Europe, and has been made increasingly valuable by its expanding data center pipeline. “Prologis shares our conviction in the long-term structural drivers underpinning demand for modern logistics and data centre infrastructure,” David Sleath, CEO of Segro, said in a statement. “We believe the combination would bring together two highly complementary businesses and create a compelling platform, combining Segro’s exceptional portfolio and development pipeline with Prologis’ existing European business and global scale, customer franchise and operational capabilities, while retaining a shared commitment to disciplined capital allocation, customers and people,” Sleath added. Prologis’ European footprint is projected to grow by 47 percent with a 368 million-square-foot regional operating portfolio. The deal anticipates a combined European development pipeline of 13 million square feet and a 126 percent increase in Prologis’ European land bank. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to legal, regulatory and Segro shareholder approvals. bullets: Prologis acquires Segro (UK REIT) for $18.8B; combined AUM ~$269B.
Segro portfolio: 117M sf UK/Europe, expanding data center pipeline.
Industrial/logistics REIT consolidation; multifamily not affected.
stories.summary: Prologis, the world's largest industrial landlord, successfully acquired rival Segro, the UK's largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro's equity at approximately $18.8 billion. The combined portfolio will total approximately $269 billion in assets under management. Segro's portfolio spans 117 million square feet across the UK and Europe with an expanding data center pipeline.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. This is an industrial/logistics REIT consolidation driven by data center demand and European logistics scarcity. It does not affect U.S. apartment supply, demand, capital availability, or construction costs.

stories.title: Blue Owl’s Stack Infrastructure Buys Virginia Data Center Site for $66M
stories.excerpt: Blue Owl Capital is pushing beyond Northern Virginia’s Data Center Alley after acquiring a 71-acre development site in Culpeper, Va., for $66.4 million. Blue Owl’s data center operator Stack Infrastructure purchased Culpeper Technology Park at 15140 Keyser Road from RACM. The transaction is equal to more than $935,000 per acre. Greysteel arranged the sale for the seller and announced the deal Tuesday. The property is in the Culpeper Tech Zone, a county-designated data center corridor with significant power infrastructure and electrical capacity. The site has by-right zoning for data center development and access to multiple fiber networks. The zone also offers county tax incentives. Culpeper is about 60 miles southwest from the center of the world’s largest data center market. The competition for that hub has pushed developers and some of the nation’s biggest investment firms to expand into surrounding Virginia markets, especially as land, power and fiber capacity become more difficult to secure. “Culpeper has moved from a speculative secondary market to an institutional-grade destination in a short window,” Greysteel Senior Director Zach Benlemlih said in a statement. “The demand for entitled, power-proximate land in the Mid-Atlantic has only intensified as Northern Virginia supply tightens, and this transaction is a direct reflection of that.” Greysteel has completed seven transactions in Culpeper, including representing the seller when it originally acquired the technology park site, as well as other data center properties and land for industrial uses. “As primary markets price out all but the most liquid buyers, well-positioned secondary sites with entitled land, fiber and power access are commanding real institutional attention,” Lacey Willard, Greysteel’s executive vice president, said. bullets: Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure acquires 71-acre data center site, Culpeper VA, $66.4M.
$935K per acre; Culpeper Tech Zone with by-right zoning, power, fiber.
Developer expansion south of Northern Virginia Data Center Alley on power/land scarcity.
stories.summary: Blue Owl Capital's Stack Infrastructure acquired a 71-acre development site (Culpeper Technology Park) in Culpeper, Virginia, for $66.4M ($935K per acre) from RACM. The property benefits from by-right data center zoning within the Culpeper Tech Zone, significant power infrastructure, fiber network access, and county tax incentives. Culpeper is approximately 60 miles southwest of Northern Virginia's data center hub.
stories.impact: Not material to multifamily. Data center site acquisition in Culpeper reflects scarcity of available land and power in Northern Virginia's primary markets, driving regional expansion. No direct signal on apartment supply, demand, or capital flows, though potential indirect wage/employment benefits if data center development drives regional job growth.
